title: Context Lake: the shared-state layer for multi-agent systems
thesis: Multi-agent systems need a shared, temporal, governed context layer (a 'context lake') distinct from vector stores and per-agent memory.
audience: AI engineers and SRE/platform teams building multi-agent systems in production

questions.question: What is a context lake, who coined the term, and how is it defined?
How does shared context for agents differ from vector databases, data lakes, feature stores and per-agent memory frameworks?
Which systems implement shared or temporal context for agents today, and what do they claim or measure?
What failures in multi-agent systems come from inconsistent or missing shared context, and what is the evidence?
queries: why do multi-agent LLM systems fail

questions.question: What are the criticisms, open problems and adoption signals for context layers in agent systems?
